* [[Lenovo|Lenovo Group]], the largest [[Peoples Republic of China|Chinese]] computer company [[Acquisition of the IBM PC business by Lenovo|acquires the personal computer business]] of [[IBM]] for [[United States dollar|US$]] 1.25 billion in cash, and Lenovo assumes $500 million of IBM's debt. [https://web.archive.org/web/20050911104111/http://today.reuters.co.uk/news/newsArticle.aspx?type=businessNews&storyID=2005-05-01T210430Z_01_CAS175695_RTRUKOC_0_TECH-LENOVO-IBM.xml (Reuters)]
* More than thirty [[Iraqis]] are killed and more than fifty are wounded as a [[bomb]] goes off at a funeral. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/40-killed-in-terror-attacks-in-iraq-1.552676 (CBC)]   
* The [[United States]] informs [[Japan]] that [[North Korea]] may have [[List of North Korean missile tests|launched]] another test [[ballistic missile|missile]] towards the [[Sea of Japan]]. The report is now said to be confirmed. [http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory?id=718761 (ABC News)] [https://www.forbes.com/work/feeds/afx/2005/05/01/afx1988520.html (Forbes)]
* [[Astronomer]]s have [[Discoveries of exoplanets|directly]] [[2M1207b|confirmed]] the existence of an extrasolar [[planet]] orbiting the [[brown dwarf]] numbered [[2M1207a]]. The team says that this is the first-ever infrared view of an [[exoplanet]]. [http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/nationworld/2002258224_planet30.html (Seattle Times)] [https://web.archive.org/web/20050430225643/http://www.eso.org/outreach/press-rel/pr-2005/pr-12-05-p2.html (ESO)] [http://cnews.canoe.ca/CNEWS/Science/2005/04/30/1019331-ap.html (CP)]
* [[Taiwan|Taiwanese]] [[President of Taiwan|president]] [[Chen Shui-bian]] requests that the [[Government of China|Chinese government]] meet directly with his government after [[China]] meets with Taiwan's opposition leader, [[Lien Chan]].  Taiwan and China are in conflict over Taiwan's increased calls for independence from the mainland. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/taiwan-s-president-calls-for-direct-talks-with-china-1.538876 (CBC)] [http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory?id=718836 (ABC)]
* [[Iraq]]i and [[United States|American]] militaries hold several suspects for questioning in the [[Margaret Hassan]] [[Kidnapping and killing of Margaret Hassan|kidnapping case]].  Hassan, director of [[Cooperative for Assistance and Relief Everywhere|CARE]]'s Iraq division, was kidnapped by insurgents in late October [[2004]] and subsequently believed to be killed. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/iraqi-forces-find-belongings-of-abducted-aid-worker-1.535069 (CBC)] [https://www.npr.org/2005/05/01/4626704/suspects-held-in-aid-workers-murder (NPR)]
* In [[Nepal]], 10,000 [[protest]]ers march in [[Kathmandu]] against the policies of king [[Gyanendra of Nepal|Gyanendra]] and demand return of [[democracy]]. {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050502165626/http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory?id=718684 |date=2 May 2005}}
* [[Italy]] intends to publish its own view of the killing of [[Nicola Calipari]]. Italian media has released classified details about a report the [[United States]] made. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/4504589.stm (BBC)]
* [[Honduras|Honduran]] [[President of Honduras|president]] [[Ricardo Maduro]], and his daughter survive with minor injuries when their plane crashes into the sea near [[Tela]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/honduran-leader-survives-plane-crash-1.553250 (CBC)] [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/americas/4504641.stm (BBC)]
